U0300.title: Internal Control Module Software Incompatibility
U0300.description: A control module has detected that its software version is incompatible with another module on the bus. Most often after a partial update, mismatched coding, or fitting a used module from a different vehicle.

causes.label: Software/calibration mismatch between modules
Used module from different vehicle fitted
Incomplete or interrupted module flash

symptoms: Multiple warning lights may illuminate
Affected modules may go into limp mode or shut down
Specific functions inoperative depending on module
Diagnostic tools may show communication faults

U0304.title: Software Incompatibility With Gear Shift Control Module
U0304.description: U0304 is stored when a control unit, usually the transmission controller, finds that the software or calibration identity of the gear shift control module does not match what it expects. GM's generic U03xx procedure (Saab 9-5, 2011) treats such codes as configuration faults: checked at 9-16 V with normal bus traffic, no circuit test, cured by setup or programming. Allison uses U0304 for its 6th-generation controls as Gear Shift Module 1 Incompatible: a 6th-generation push-button selector does not work with a 5th-generation TCM, and the selector must match the TCM calibration; U0333 covers selector 2. U0103 means lost contact, U0404 invalid data from the same module. The driver may be unable to select a range.

causes.label: Shift selector generation or type does not match the TCM calibration (e.g. after replacement)
Shift module or TCM replaced or flashed without setup
Software update aborted, wrong file loaded

symptoms: Gear ranges cannot be selected or the selector does not respond
Transmission warning or code shown on the selector display
Code appears right after a selector or TCM was replaced

U0308.title: Software Incompatibility With Throttle Actuator Control Module
U0308.description: U0308 flags that the throttle actuator control module carries software or a calibration that the engine controller does not accept. In most current cars throttle control lives inside the ECM/PCM, so a separate TAC module and this code are rare; no manufacturer documents U0308 publicly. Ford shows how such a mismatch is handled when the logic is integrated: its 2012 OBD summary files a software version mismatch between the electronic-throttle processors under U0300, non-MIL on Gen2 and MIL on Gen3/Gen4 throttle systems. GM's U03xx procedure links these codes to a module that was not configured after installation. Throttle control affects emissions, so CARB demands monitoring and a MIL is likely. U0107 means lost contact, U0408 invalid data.

causes.label: Throttle or engine control module replaced or flashed without matching software
Wrong or outdated calibration loaded, e.g. by an engine tune
Programming aborted due to low voltage

symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced power or limp mode with limited throttle opening
Code appears after module replacement or programming

U0316.title: Software Incompatibility With Vehicle Dynamics Control Module
U0316.description: U0316 means the vehicle dynamics control module, the electronic stability control unit, reports a software or calibration identity another module does not accept, typically after it was replaced or reflashed without setup. GM's U03xx procedure (Saab 9-5, 2011) runs at 9-16 V and sets such codes when a module is not configured properly; GM itself uses U0315 for its electronic brake module. Mazda uses U0316 differently: in 2014-2015 Mazda3, Mazda6 and CX-5 bulletins U0316:09 sits in a receiving module and stands for an error signal received from the DSC unit, there caused by a failed SAS module. So on a Mazda it is a follow-up code, not a software issue. U0122 means lost contact, U0416 invalid data. Stability control may switch off; MIL normally off.

causes.label: Stability control module replaced or flashed without setup/coding
Software variant does not match vehicle equipment
Mazda: fault in DSC or SAS module reported to other units (U0316:09)

symptoms: Stability or traction control warning light on
Driver assistance functions unavailable
Code stored in several modules at once

U0317.title: Software Incompatibility With Park Brake Control Module
U0317.description: U0317 tells that the park brake control module of an electric parking brake runs software or a calibration another module does not accept. Following GM's generic U03xx logic it is checked at 9-16 V with normal bus traffic, sets when a module is not configured properly and needs no wiring test; the cure is setup or programming. No manufacturer documents this J2012 meaning publicly. Mitsubishi reassigns the number: for the 2017 Outlander (TSB-17-23-001) U0317 stands for a CAN time-out with the EPB ECU, which a wrongly programmed TCM stored as P0317 instead; a TCM reflash corrects it. On such vehicles read U0317 as a communication fault. U0128 means lost contact, U0417 invalid data. Park brake warnings or disabled auto functions are possible; no MIL.

causes.label: Park brake module replaced or flashed without setup
Mitsubishi: CAN time-out to the EPB ECU, e.g. connector unplugged
Software level of park brake module and partner module do not match

symptoms: Park brake warning light or message
Automatic release or hill hold not working
Code appears after park brake module work

U0318.title: Software Incompatibility With Brake System Control Module
U0318.description: U0318 indicates a software or calibration mismatch with the brake system control module, a unit J2012 separates from the ABS module (U0315) and the vehicle dynamics module (U0316). Which box that is depends on the maker; on brake-by-wire systems or electromechanical boosters it is often the controller that builds brake pressure. GM's U03xx procedure (Saab 9-5, 2011) describes the trigger: a module not configured properly, checked at 9-16 V, no external circuit involved. No manufacturer documents U0318 publicly, so the exact owner of the code must come from the vehicle's own manual. It mostly appears after a module swap or a broken flash. U0129 means lost contact, U0418 invalid data. Brake warnings and reduced assist functions are possible; MIL usually off.

causes.label: Brake system module replaced or flashed without setup
Software level does not match the ABS/ESC or engine controller
Programming aborted due to low battery voltage

symptoms: Brake system warning light or message
Brake assist or regenerative braking functions unavailable
Code appears after brake module service

U0319.title: Software Incompatibility With Steering Effort Control Module
U0319.description: U0319 is set when the steering effort control module, the unit that varies steering assist, for example with road speed, reports a software or calibration identity the network does not accept. J2012 keeps it apart from the power steering control module, which has its own code U0320. GM's generic U03xx description fits: the check runs at 9-16 V with normal bus traffic, and a module that was not configured after installation sets the code; the repair is programming, not wiring. No manufacturer documents U0319 publicly, so which steering unit carries the code is maker-specific. U0130 means lost contact, U0419 invalid data from the same module. Steering may feel heavier or less speed-dependent, a steering warning may light, the MIL normally stays off.

causes.label: Steering module replaced or flashed without setup
Software variant does not match vehicle configuration
Programming aborted or wrong file loaded

symptoms: Steering heavier or assist no longer speed-dependent
Steering warning light or message
Code appears after steering module work
